_meta.description: Whole loot RESULTS observed on retail ENEMIES, keyed by the lootTable id the enemy rolled against.
_meta.authoritative: every result here appeared verbatim in a retail response from https://blades.bgs.services/; nothing is interpolated or invented
_meta.derivation: dungeonGeneratedDataList -> enemyGeneratedData -> lootTableLoot, mined from captured retail traffic. A result is the COMPLETE set of things one roll produced, kept whole, so a re-roll reproduces what retail produced together; per-item frequencies cannot express that and could never yield more than a single stack.
_meta.emptyResultIsReal: an enemy that dropped nothing is an observed outcome and must be drawn like any other; removing it would inflate every drop rate in this file
_meta.instanceIdsStripped: items[].id is a uuid4 minted per drop and has been removed -- the consumer MUST mint a fresh one per drop. properties.GRADING/ENCHANTING[].id are shared property DEFINITION ids and are kept.
_meta.howToDraw: pick the table entry, then: if levelKeyed is false use `results`; if true pick the `byLevel` band whose [minEnemyLevel, maxEnemyLevel] contains the enemy's level, or the nearest band if none does, and use its `results`. Exactly one of `results` and `byLevel` is non-null. Draw one whole result weighted by `n`. A table absent from this file was never observed often enough to model: drop nothing.
_meta.levelKeying: measured, not assumed. The drop RATE is level-flat -- the empty-result rate moves less than 6 points across level deciles on every table that has one, and stackable quantities do not correlate with level (|r| <= 0.17). The CONTENT is not: every table carrying currency pays out in proportion to enemy level (|r| >= 0.96), and gear tables gate their item templates by level (template drift 0.48-0.87). Tables are keyed by level when |currencyLevelCorrelation| >= 0.5 or templateLevelDrift >= 0.3.
_meta.insufficientLevelSpreadMeans: the table is level-dependent but held too few observations to fill two bands, so its single band spans every level it was seen at and a draw will NOT respect level scaling. Flagged rather than dropped, because some retail-observed loot beats none; treat it as the weakest data here.
_meta.deduplication: on (questId, sha1 of the dungeon entry). The same generated dungeon is re-served in dozens of responses (54.3% of entries seen were re-serves) and would otherwise weight a table by how often a player opened the quest screen.

spawnGroupLoot.note: a bare loot result, NOT keyed by a group id. Retail barely used it and every observation is the same single item, so it is recorded here and not modelled.

control.provenance: only https://blades.bgs.services was mined; our own server's replayed traffic was excluded. Retail shut down 2026-06-30.

positive.expected: high -- this is the gold table

negative.expected: near zero -- stackable items only, nothing to scale
